Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Aurora Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Aurora Infra Lead), Jasmin Li (Aurora CTO)
summary: Discovery focused on latency & throughput requirements for Aurora Payments. Customer targets: p95 latency 200-400ms for single-turn customer support completions, concurrency up to 250 concurrent sessions, streaming required for partial responses. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs, security needs (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), and a next-step performance benchmark across model sizes.
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're excited to dig into your latency and throughput needs today
[00:08] Priya Patel: thanks, Sophie. to start, we're building an ai first support flow—short prompts, mostly 30-120 tokens each, we need answers back fast, p95 is our key SLO.
[00:20] Marco Diaz: cool, quick q on that SLO, do you have a numeric target today? p95 across which window, like full-response or first-streamed token?
[00:28] Priya: yeah sorry, p95 full response, target is around 250-400ms for 90% of flows, for higher-quality fallbacks maybe 500ms is tolerable but prefer under 400.
[00:38] Tom Reynolds: and concurrency, we're expecting bursty traffic—roughly 200-250 concurrent sessions during peak, each session doing 2-3 short calls per minute, plus background batch jobs for embeddings.
[00:50] Marco: ok, that's helpful. for streaming use cases, p95 is usually measured to first byte, which helps. our hosted offering does streaming very efficiently, but the tradeoffs you care about are cost and predictable throughput—Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools.
[01:05] Jasmin Li: hi, I just jumped in — curious about private deployment options too, data residency and KMS integration are musts for us.
[01:12] Sophie: noted — we'll include Private/VPC things in the security pack. quick question back to Priya: what models are you considering? open models only or mixing with closed models?
[01:22] Priya: open models primarily. We want the flexibility to move between smaller low-latency models for common queries and bigger models for escalations. ideally a canary-fallback flow.
[01:32] Marco: yep that's a common pattern — route ~85% to 7B/13B low-latency variants, escalate to 70B for the hard ones. in terms of raw tokens-per-second, rough numbers we've seen: 7B on modern T4/A10-like hardware in our runtime can do ~300-800 tokens/sec depending on batching and sequence length; 13B tends to be 150-350 tps; 70B is more like 25-80 tps. these are ballpark and depend on quantization/profile.
[01:55] Tom: ok that's useful. what about p95 latencies at our concurrency? if we have 250 concurrent sessions, can hosted meet 300-400ms p95?
[02:05] Marco: it depends — streaming helps a lot for perceived latency because first-byte can be under 100-150ms for small prompts. end-to-end full-response p95 at 250 concurrency on hosted might be tight for 70B, but with model routing (7B for majority) and batching windows tuned, hosted often meets sub-400ms for 7B/13B. Dedicated gives more predictable tail latencies since capacity is reserved.
[02:28] Priya: can you explain batching windows? we've seen that batching reduces cost but increases tail latency.
[02:35] Marco: sure — our runtime does continuous batching with dynamic batch windows that consider request arrival rates. for short prompts and streaming, we can batch very aggressively with tiny windows (5-10ms) to keep p95 low; for throughput-focused batch jobs we use larger windows. the platform also uses prefix/KV cache, so repeated prefixes (like standard system prompts) don't redo full compute, which improves p95 at scale.
[02:58] Jasmin: you said KV cache — sometimes in our infra notes people write it as KV cash, so don't worry if transcripts flip it. does that require sticky routing?
[03:06] Marco: good call — cache locality is handled by routing and session affinity for best perf; for Dedicated we can guarantee higher cache hit rates by pinning sessions to worker pools.
[03:16] Sophie: Priya, what are your availability / SLA expectations? and any compliance red flags?
[03:21] Priya: SLA we'd like 99.9 for production. compliance — SOC2 required, SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS/HSM support, audit logs for prompts/response redaction controls. Also data retention policies — we need logs for 180 days but want PII redaction.
[03:38] Sophie: we'll include SOC2 and the SAML/KMS docs. for on-prem/Private we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations, and audit logs with configurable retention.
[03:47] Tom: for benchmarking, can you run our real prompts? we have about 20 representative prompt templates and synthetic concurrency profile.
[03:54] Marco: yes, we can run a token/sec and latency benchmark across 7B/13B/70B; typically we run: single-request latency, p50/p95/p99, and sustained throughput for 15-30m at target concurrency. we'll need sample payloads + target SLAs.
[04:10] Priya: perfect. what's the usual lead time for a dedicated capacity pilot?
[04:14] Sophie: dedicated pilots typically take 1-2 weeks to provision depending on GPU availability and your region; Private/VPC deployments are 2-4 weeks plus security reviews. the quickest path is Hosted trial while we run benchmarks, then switch to Dedicated if tails are an issue.
[04:30] Jasmin: cost is also a factor — can you share rough TCO tradeoffs? e.g., hosted vs dedicated monthly for our concurrency and usage mix?
[04:37] Sophie: absolutely — I'll send a TCO sheet. example: for a workload that's 85% 7B at peak concurrency 250, the per-token hosted cost is lower to start but with sustained high qps Dedicated often wins on effective cost per request due to reserved capacity and better batch efficiency. we'll show modeled numbers in the TCO.
[04:55] Tom: any gotchas with streaming and tokens/sec metrics? we rely on streaming for progressive render in our web UI.
[05:01] Marco: streaming doesn't change tokens/sec on the GPU but changes perceived latency; our streaming implementation flushes partial tokens as they're generated. if you need first-byte p95 < 150ms, we tune batch windows for streaming and prefer smaller model variants to keep GPU compute time low.
[05:16] Sophie: also worth mentioning quantization options — int8 or mixed precision can increase tokens/sec significantly for 13B/70B but may need evals for quality regressions. we'll include quantization recommendations in the benchmark results.
[05:30] Priya: thanks. what about autoscaling behavior? if bursts exceed reserved capacity, will hosted auto-burst?
[05:36] Sophie: hosted will auto-burst across our pool; Dedicated has configurable burst or overprovision options. for strict performance SLAs, Dedicated + burst policy is common. also, smart routing can fallback to regional hosted instances for emergencies.
[05:50] Priya: sounds good. one last technical — how do you measure p95 for streaming vs non-streaming?
[05:56] Marco: we report both: p95 first-byte (streaming) and p95 full-response. for your UI the first-byte is most relevant, but we include both in benchmark reports so you can set alarms appropriately.
[06:10] Tom: ok let's lock next steps 
[06:12] Sophie: recap — we'll: 1) run a perf benchmark with your 20 prompts across 7B/13B/70B measuring p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and streaming first-byte latencies; 2) send hosted vs dedicated TCO and pricing; 3) share SOC2 / SAML / KMS docs and trial keys; 4) schedule a follow-up to review results next week.
[06:31] Priya: great, thanks everyone. looking forward to the benchmark.
[06:35] Jasmin: thanks all.
[06:37] [end of recording]
